title: Anthropic Lets Companies Self-Host Claude Managed Agents
dek: The full agent stack can now run inside your own cloud or servers.

facts.label: Route to Anthropic, a cloud or own gateway

caption:
Your AI agents, your servers, your rules. 🔒

Anthropic has opened a private beta that lets companies run Claude Managed Agents entirely inside their own cloud or on-premises setup. Before, only the agent sandbox could live on company hardware. Now the agent server, the session history database, the workers and the credentials can all stay behind your own security perimeter.

Teams also choose where requests to Claude go: straight to Anthropic, through Amazon Bedrock, Google's Agent Platform or Microsoft Foundry, or via their own gateway. The core APIs match the hosted version, so agents built there should carry over.

Why it matters: enterprises wanting autonomous agents on sensitive code and internal tools no longer have to build an agent platform from scratch. The trade-off is running and securing the infrastructure yourself. We're following every Claude agent update here at AI Parabellum.

Security teams just lost one of their biggest reasons to say no to AI agents.

With Anthropic's new self-hosted Claude Managed Agents beta, the control plane, credentials and session history all run in your environment, while model requests can flow through Anthropic, Bedrock, Google or Microsoft Foundry. More control, more ops work.
